# Plan: the 12 live issues of 2026-09-16 by the mechanism that produces them

Tree 46639344d5623c36a96ed27436952db3786f8084 (git rev-parse HEAD). Inputs read whole: issues-report.md, coordination-objective.md, coordination-lever.md, instrument-conventions.md. Lane MCP read first: lane_brief (records in reach: none; monitor not armed), lane_jobs (9 jobs, plan slots out/ref/scope), lane_changes (empty checkpoint); lane_findings needs a record id and none is in reach. Read only; nothing below is code.

## Part 1 — classes by mechanism
An issue appears in two classes when two mechanisms produce it; the count at the end says so.

C1. State kept as a read-then-written file or git row, with no transaction and no history. Issues 2 (the lock's by/at hold the latest claimant only; ~/.local/state/agentscient/deliverable.json is flat), 5 (ledger.py highest() L147-176 is max-over-tree-and-origin plus one; defects.py next L38 is that shim; no reservation, so two branches mint LD-68).
- Pattern: a machine on the state engine with an append-only marking, ids allocated in one transaction (objective §6).
- Carried by: machine.py (_move_locked L266-309 reads under the write lock; marking append-only); instrument-conventions §State names the lock and ledgers as declared debt (FILE_BACKED pin: control, deliverable, ladder, ledger). Nothing carries an id reservation today.
- Change: the lock becomes a `deliverable` machine with a side table; show prints the marking as history. next takes a row in a host-local reservations table before printing; add refuses an id not reserved by this session. Placement files flip file->sqlite; the gate's pin shrinks (its one invited edit).
- Cost: two levers, two placement files, two test files, the watchdog's deliverable_lock() reader (watchdog.py L848-866) and test_watchdog_deliverable.py follow the store. deliverable.py has no contract page and no registry row (git ls-files ops/conductor/registry/deliverable.py.json -> 0): the slice adds both.
- Does not cover: two hosts (store is host-local, machine-lever.md); the two LD-68s already filed (reconciled by hand before either PR merges); issue 2's "three Opus sessions" count.

C2. Authority keyed on a value the actor supplies or shares. Issues 2 (_check_actor machine.py L253-263 compares row["holder"] == agent, the WF_AGENT display string), 10 (bind-for mints a participant for a session id "no dispatch produced"; Codex/Grok have no session id).
- Pattern: participant is a system-minted id checked against the record that minted it; no verb takes the acting participant as an argument (coordination-lever §Participants, class `arguments`).
- Carried by: the coordination core (PR #243, 05b8aebe, not on dev); launch.py mints a session id per dispatch and passes --session-id.
- Change: bind-for refuses class `participant` unless the session id is carried by a dispatch record in the jobs root (_find_record, launch.py L2518-2526); the launcher sets CLAUDE_SESSION_ID for Codex and Grok workers.
- Cost: a read edge conductor tool -> launcher record shape (ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md), declared and gated; one launcher env-building change.
- Does not cover: subjects.holder stays the agent string for other machines (idea, not built); a worker that never binds.

C3. One channel carries both the observation and the conclusion. Issues 4 (watchdog reports closed history as live deviations; Watch.__init__ L892-897 suppresses `closed` lines but scan_deviations L915 still runs on them), 8 (a worker writes status=tripped itself; the launcher keeps it, so one field says "breaker fired" and "the worker chose the word").
- Pattern: status from evidence the runner holds, content from the worker; history and live reported as separate counts (probes.md).
- Carried by: monitor.py (events with own state and delivery columns); the probe runner. PR #244 (515e5b72) is issue 4's fix in review.
- Change: launcher sets envelope status from TRIPPED/breaker.log; a self-reported tripped with findings closes as the worker's verdict with note `self-reported tripped`; `deviation envelope` fires only on the launcher's own trip. Issue 4 waits on #244: no slice.
- Cost: launcher envelope parse, its test, watchdog-lever.md L115.
- Does not cover: an invalid envelope with findings (a real deviation); a worker that lies in findings.

C4. A command stored as one string and re-tokenized by a tokenizer other than the shell that would run it. Issue 3 (reading() deliverable.py L111 runs shlex.split(target["measure"]) with no shell).
- Pattern: argv as a list, never a string (launch.py builds lists; testkit.run takes argv; the wrapper test pins exact lists).
- Carried by: instrument.run(); the launcher.
- Change: --measure stored and run as a JSON list; a string measure refuses class `arguments` naming the list shape; live targets re-added by their sessions.
- Cost: one lever, its test, the skill page; live lock targets rewritten by hand.
- Does not cover: onboard's own timeouts (TIMEOUT=5, RETRY_TIMEOUT=20), never measured twice.

C5. A test guards a live host path instead of owning a hermetic world. Issue 6 (test_dispatch_wrapper.py L197-206 watches _jobs_roots_to_guard() on the host; L277-281 asserts them unchanged).
- Pattern: docs/tests.md rule 4; the launcher admits DISPATCH_JOBS (live-target refusal, launch.py L1768-1769).
- Carried by: testkit.World; the launcher.
- Change: fixture sets DISPATCH_JOBS under the world root and watches that path; host watch and LD-16 tolerance go.
- Cost: one test file. Does not cover: the other three copier suites the wall handoff names, if they watch the host too (not measured: a finding against this plan).

C6. The transport's stamp and receipt stand in for the record's. Issues 9 (stamped 09:10Z, received 08:47:46Z), 11 ("queued there" is not a receipt; hold-for-approval is real).
- Pattern: the core stamps queued_at, delivered_at, acked_at with its own clock and keeps queued/delivered/acknowledged/resolved apart (coordination-lever §Messages).
- Carried by: the coordination core (#243); instrument.now(). Change: none beyond landing #243; the harness msg_id is delivery_ref, never the clock.
- Cost: nothing new. Does not cover: the harness's own stamp skew (only measurable beside the core's); idle-session wakeup (no channels facility in Claude Code 2.1.273).

C7. The launcher infers the target from where it is run. Issue 7 (_launch L1761-1763 refuses unless branch == lineage; record copies land in the cwd repo's .dev/records/dispatches, L1872).
- Pattern: target named as data (--lineage with --ref), record written to the jobs root, copied to the branch by land.py at landing.
- Carried by: the launcher already takes --lineage and --ref; land.py already copies records onto the lineage.
- Change: from a checkout on the trunk, --lineage lane/session-* that exists is admitted; the checkout is never written; landing copies the record. I-010 is the gate.
- Cost: launcher, land.py, CONTRACT.md, test_launch_lane_conf.py, test_launch_record_copy.py, test_land_lever.py. Highest risk: dispatcher and argv.
- Does not cover: _collect/_close L2700, L2859 keep the same check until the record carries the lineage.

C8. Permission decided by matching command text, outside the lever. Issues 1 (classifier denied hand.py declare as "Self-Modification"; chat "approved" passed the identical command), 12 (210 hook misses today, 191 `refused`; clipped-sweep 55, done-gate 51, claim-unmeasured 42), and issue 10's unmeasured premise that hooks cannot see MCP calls. This run added one: the file-state hook refused this plan's own out/PLAN.md.
- Pattern: authority inside the function it guards, hooks as feedback only (coordination-lever §Conventions); the vendor classifier as an external surface with contract, probe and mock (verified-couplings §External surfaces).
- Carried by: the coordination core's design; harness-capabilities.md; the refused skill; skills.py miss telemetry.
- Change: a probe row for the classifier edge (command, denial text, chat-approval remedy) in harness-capabilities.md; the refused skill names the remedy; the hook-blindness claim is measured by a probe before a design rests on it; the file-state hook admits a dispatch job's declared outputs (jobs.json outputs) under the state directory.
- Cost: two pages, a probe row, one hook edit under a wall grant. Does not cover: the miss rate itself (falls only when each top class gets a lever that does the compliant thing by default); the classifier's model.
